faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium dental abutment?
faq.a: Grade 23 ELI (ASTM F136) is the standard for dental implants. Better fatigue performance than CP grades and essential for osseointegration. Never substitute industrial Grade 5.

faq.q: How is a titanium dental abutment manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium dental abutment is manufactured using VAR melting; Closed-die hot forging; CNC swiss turning; Thread rolling. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM F136) for titanium dental abutment?
faq.a: Other materials such as steel or aluminum are significantly heavier and lack the corrosion resistance required for long-term service.

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium dental abutment?
faq.a: Titanium Dental Abutment components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium dental abutment?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Internal hex drive tolerance +-0.02mm required for driver engagement; Surface contamination (Fe, Ni) must be <0.05% per ASTM F86. Proper material selection, manufacturing process control, and inspection mitigate these risks.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium dental abutment?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
